title: Minimum Score of a Path Between Two Cities
summary: Given n cities numbered 1 to n and a 2D array roads indicating bidirectional roads with distances, find the minimum score of a path between cities 1 and n.
statement: Given n cities numbered 1 to n and a 2D array roads indicating bidirectional roads with distances, find the minimum score of a path between cities 1 and n. The score is the minimum distance in the path. The cities graph is not necessarily connected. A path can include the same road multiple times, and cities 1 and n can be visited multiple times. There is at least one path between cities 1 and n.
constraints: Roads are undirected and at least one path connects city 1 to city n.
A path may repeat vertices and roads; its score is the minimum road distance used.
Return the smallest score achievable by any path from 1 to n.
hints: Traverse the entire connected component containing city 1.
Track the minimum distance of every incident road seen in that component.
Because walks may repeat edges, a route from 1 can detour through the minimum edge and then continue to n.
Thus every component edge can determine an achievable score, and no path can score below the minimum component edge.
editorial: Thus every component edge can determine an achievable score, and no path can score below the minimum component edge.

tests.explanation: All cities are connected to city 1, and the smallest road in that component has distance five, which can be included in a walk to city 4.
The sole road is required, so the path score is ten.
